title: CardCorpus moved addresses
description: Every address that was published and no longer resolves, and what became of it: merged into another, moved to another, split into several (every successor, none picked), or removed. An id never changes once published and a retired address is never given to anything else, so a consumer only needs this file when a stored pointer stops resolving. Each successor is the current address, any chain already followed (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#identifiers).

moved.description: Every retired address, with what became of it.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `catalog` or `set` or `card` or `variant` or `painting`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

set.description: The set's id (sets/{catalog}.json). On a `card` and a `variant`: the set it is in; on an old `painting` address, its first print's set.

card.description: The card's id, unique in its set. On a `variant`: the card it is of.

id.description: Its own id: the catalog's (index.json's `catalogs`; every set, card and variant id under an old catalog's is read under the new one's), the set's (sets/{catalog}.json), the card's in its set, the variant's among its card's, or the painting's (a painting address with a `set` is an old one, named for its first print's card, from before paintings had ids of their own).

merged.description: The address it was merged into.
